lines.text: Your cab costs triple when it rains. This girl lost a month of fares before she found out why.
No car. One umbrella. Same tech park as half her lane.
Rainy Monday one. One and a half times. Analysts blame drizzle.
Monday three. Triple. Her umbrella files for bankruptcy.
So Priya wades to the main road, to book from a cheaper pin.
The umbrella flips. Still triple. Now also soaked.
Then her driver, Raju, says the quiet part.
Madam, four people book from your gate. Same minute. Same tech park.
Rohan. Arjun. Sharma ji. And you.
The demand pumping her surge? Her own neighbours.
Lesson: when the whole lane rides alone, the whole lane pays triple.
So the four pooled up on an app. Arjun drives.
The live map shows exactly how far his car is.
Nobody waits in the rain. They step out when it's at the gate.
Closing bell. Priya's fare, flat. Her umbrella, out of bankruptcy.
Whole lane paying surge? Pool it on Sahyatri. Link in bio.
